content.text:
I checked every 2025 required minimum distribution (RMD). All of them were taken in full, from the right accounts, in November and December 2025. That is well before the 1 April 2026 deadline.

**Who owes an RMD.** Prema Raghavan was born on 22 July 1952, so she turned 73 in 2025. That makes 2025 her first RMD year, with a deadline of 1 April 2026. She retired from Hollins and Reade in January 2020, so the 401(k)'s exception for people still working there doesn't apply. Martin Kessler was born in 1957 and owes nothing yet. Martin is her sole beneficiary and is less than 10 years younger, so the IRS Uniform Lifetime Table applies. Its factor for age 73 is 26.5.

**How much each account owed.** Each RMD is the account's balance on 31 December 2024 divided by 26.5. The balances come from the custodian's position and cash files.

| Account | 31 Dec 2024 balance | 2025 RMD |
|---|---|---|
| SYN-58140002 Traditional IRA | $582,446.94 | $21,979.13 |
| SYN-58140003 Rollover IRA | $194,775.76 | $7,350.03 |
| SYN-58140004 401(k) | $311,957.24 | $11,771.97 |

**What was taken.**
- **IRAs:** RMDs from several IRAs can be taken from any one of them. Together the two IRAs owed $29,329.16. On 4 December 2025 exactly $29,329.16 was paid out of SYN-58140002, which matches the Form 1099-R and the instruction she signed on 24 November 2025.
- **401(k):** RMDs from a 401(k) can't be combined with IRAs and have to come from the plan itself. On 5 November 2025 exactly $11,771.97 was paid from the plan, which matches its Form 1099-R.
- **Cash check:** The cash movements in both accounts add up to the year-end cash balances. Both payouts were the full amounts before tax withholding, so nothing was short.
